# Gate 7: Sprint 1 (MVP: S-1, S-2, S-3)

The MVP is done. All three Must stories are accepted, merged into `main`, and green on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. **We're over the 2–4 hour time budget, so I need your call on Sprint 2's scope** (see the decisions at the end).

**Delivered:**

| Story | QA | CI evidence | Merge |
|---|---|---|---|
| S-1 Score and pass/fail verdict | PASS 8/8, 0 defects | run 37764220926 | `126b382` |
| S-2 Marks short of or above the pass mark | PASS 8/8, 300 random inputs with 0 mismatches | run 37796019119 | `9b56aac` |
| S-3 Clear messages for invalid entries | PASS 8/8, 179-check edge sweep | run 37797412005 | `4b63578` |

- **`main` now:** [CI run 37799155672](https://github.com/Sabeekhann/Web-Calculator/actions/runs/37799155672) passes 131 unit tests, plus 31 browser tests on each of Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (93 in total), on Node 20.
- **Accessibility:** 0 violations in every state.
- **Sprint log:** `sprint-log.md` has the Sprint 1 review and retro.

**Agents used:**
- developer: 3 stories, tests first each time.
- qa-engineer: 3 independent verifications.
- ux-ui-designer: 3 visual reviews.
- docs-writer: the sprint log.

**Issues in the sprint and how they were handled:**
- **QA agent cut off by the usage limit:** the first S-1 QA run hit the account usage limit and was re-run after it reset.
- **My CI mistake:** a screenshot push I made cancelled the CI run on S-2's code. QA caught it and used the next green run, which had identical code. Screenshots now go in with the QA report.
- **Cosmetic items queued for Sprint 2 polish:** a lone word wrapping onto the gap line's second line on phones, and a small gap after the minus in "-5".

**Retro, what changes:**
- Screenshots never land between a code commit and its QA.
- QA always signs off against a green CI run on the exact commit it tested.
- Your real-browser checks are scheduled before release.

**Deliverables touched:**
- D1, D4 and D5 are IN PROGRESS.
- D6 is IN PROGRESS: visual reviews passed, polish is pending.
- All three stories are still marked "Not implemented" in `user-stories.md` until your real-browser checks are done, as the honesty rule requires.

**Time:**
- Sprint 1 ran 10:23–15:17 UTC (294 min). That includes your review time and a pause while the usage limit reset.
- **The total since preflight is about 7h10m of elapsed time**, well beyond the brief's 2–4 hours.
- I'd present that honestly in the submission: the elapsed time includes review waits and the usage-limit pause, and isn't hands-on effort.

**Decisions for you:**
1. **Sprint 2 scope.** I recommend option **(b)**. The MVP already meets the brief, and option (b) keeps quality while respecting the budget.
   - **(a) Full plan:** S-4 "Next learner" (the Should story), plus the hardening sweep, accessibility audit and polish. About 45–60 min including QA.
   - **(b) Cut S-4, which the rules allow** ("cut Should stories, never quality"): do only the polish and final hardening, then go to release. About 25–30 min. S-4 stays honestly "Not implemented". The "Next learner" button and "or press Esc" hint currently do nothing, so I'd remove them from the screen until S-4 exists.
2. **Live URL.** Your real-browser checks need either a local run on your machine or GitHub Pages (free, D3). Turning on Pages now would let you check all three stories in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari while Sprint 2 runs. Shall I?

**GitHub:** branch `main`, commit [`bfcaf41`](https://github.com/Sabeekhann/Web-Calculator/commit/bfcaf41), pushed: yes.

**Awaiting:** "approved", plus (a) or (b), and yes or no on Pages.

## Manual checks for the PO — final real-browser checklist
Open https://sabeekhann.github.io/Web-Calculator/ after this build is merged to `main`. Do steps 1–11 in **Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari** (desktop); steps 12–14 once on a phone (or desktop window made narrow).
1. Load the page. **Expect:** tab title "Quiz score and pass-mark calculator", a small icon on the tab, pass mark shows "70", the score area says "Enter marks earned and total marks possible to see the score." There is no "Next learner" button and no "or press Esc" text.
2. Type 17.5 in Marks earned and 23 in Total marks possible (don't press anything). **Expect:** "76.0%", "Pass", "1.4 marks above the pass mark".
3. Change Marks earned to 15.5. **Expect:** "67.3%", "Fail", "0.6 marks short of the pass mark". Then change the pass mark to 65. **Expect:** "Pass", score stays "67.3%".
4. Watch the bottom edge of the white card while you do step 3 and steps 6–7. **Expect:** it never jumps up or down.
5. Set pass mark 70 again, then enter 17.5 of 25. **Expect:** "70.0%", "Pass", "Exactly on the pass mark". Then 17.49 of 25. **Expect:** "69.9%", "Fail" (never "70.0%").
6. (S-1/S-2 error) Enter 23.5 of 23. **Expect:** red message under Marks earned "Marks earned can't be more than the total marks possible.", score area "The score will appear once every entry is valid.", no score. Change Marks earned to 17.5. **Expect:** message gone, "76.0%", "Pass".
7. (S-3 error) Type abc in Marks earned and 0 in Total. **Expect:** "Marks earned must be a number, like 17.5." and "Total marks possible must be more than 0." both show, no score.
8. Put 17.5 of 23 back and clear the pass mark. **Expect:** "76.0%" stays, "Enter a pass mark to see whether this is a pass or a fail.", no Pass/Fail, no red message.
9. Copy the text ` 17.5 ` (with spaces) from anywhere and paste it into Marks earned (total 23, pass 70). **Expect:** "76.0%", "Pass".
10. Click into Marks earned, then press Tab repeatedly. **Expect:** a visible blue outline moves Marks earned → Total marks possible → Pass mark, then leaves the card (to the browser bar); Shift+Tab goes back. Nothing gets stuck.
11. Switch your computer to dark mode (Windows: Settings > Personalization > Colors > Dark; Mac: System Settings > Appearance > Dark) and reload. **Expect:** dark card, all text and the red/green states easy to read. Reload also empties the fields and resets the pass mark to "70".
12. Phone: tap Marks earned. **Expect:** a number keypad with a decimal point opens.
13. Phone: enter 16.08 of 23 with pass mark 69.9. **Expect:** "69.9%", "Pass", "Less than 0.01 marks above the pass mark"; no sideways scrolling, nothing cut off.
14. Phone: enter -5 in the pass mark. **Expect:** "Pass mark can't be negative." and no score.

Report any step that differs (browser + step number + what you saw).

## Verdict: PASS

content.text:
# Gate 8: Sprint 2 (polish, hardening, live URL)

Sprint 2 is done and merged into `main`, and the live site now serves the final build. QA found no defects. What's left before release is your real-browser checklist below.

**Delivered:**
- **Live URL:** **https://sabeekhann.github.io/Web-Calculator/** is deployed from `main` on every push. The Pages run on `10af8a8` succeeded.
- **S-4 removed from the screen:** the S-4 story was cut (DEC-17), so the "Next learner" button and "or press Esc" hint are gone. The design spec, mockup, test plan and backlog all say so.
- **Polish:**
  - Better line wrapping in the gap line and the subheading.
  - "-5" no longer looks like "- 5".
  - The space held for the result is now tighter, and nothing on the card shifts.
  - There's a favicon.
- **Hardening:**
  - The accessibility scan (axe, WCAG 2.2 AA) now runs on 5 states in light and dark.
  - The full edge sweep is automated (E-EDGE.0–9): pasted values, 400-digit inputs, repeated Enter, reload, and typing key by key.
  - Both run on all 3 engines in CI.
- **`main` now** ([CI on `10af8a8`](https://github.com/Sabeekhann/Web-Calculator/actions)): 131 unit tests, and 51 browser tests on each of Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (153 in total), 0 failed, on Node 20.
- **QA hardening checks (H-1 to H-15), all PASS:**
  - Keyboard-only use works, with no focus traps.
  - Screen-reader labels, live updates and error links are correct.
  - Reduced motion is respected.
  - The page fits 320px wide.
  - There are no console errors.

The final screenshots are above.

**Agents used:**
- **developer:** the Pages workflow, polish, accessibility tests, edge tests and the 3 small design fixes.
- **ux-ui-designer:** polish review (3 small findings, applied), spec and mockup aligned, final screenshots.
- **solution-architect:** aligned the plans and added ADR-010 for Pages.
- **qa-engineer:** final hardening (PASS).
- **docs-writer:** the Sprint 2 log.

**Issues found in review:**
- **Missing tests:** the architect found that the edge tests planned at Stage 5 had never been written. They're now automated.
- **Two wrong claims:** the architect also said the polish CSS was missing and Q-13 was still open. I checked both and rejected them.
- **Tight layout margin:** the space held for the result has only 1–1.5px to spare. It passes in CI, but CI runs Linux fonts, while Windows and Mac fonts are sized differently. **Step 4 below watches for this.**

**Your real-browser checklist:** open the live URL. Do steps 1–11 in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, and steps 12–14 on a phone.
1. Load the page. Tab title "Quiz score and pass-mark calculator", an icon on the tab, pass mark "70", the "Enter marks earned…" prompt. **No** "Next learner" button.
2. Enter 17.5 and 23. You should see "76.0%", "Pass", "1.4 marks above the pass mark".
3. Change earned to 15.5: "67.3%", "Fail", "0.6 marks short…". Then change the pass mark to 65: "Pass", and the score stays 67.3%.
4. **While doing step 3 and steps 6–7, watch the bottom edge of the white card. It should never jump.**
5. Pass mark back to 70. Enter 17.5 of 25: "70.0%", "Pass", "Exactly on the pass mark". Then 17.49 of 25: "69.9%", "Fail".
6. Enter 23.5 of 23: a red message under Marks earned, "The score will appear once every entry is valid.", and no score. Fix it to 17.5: back to 76.0% Pass.
7. Type "abc" in earned and "0" in total: both fields show their own message.
8. Back to 17.5 of 23, then clear the pass mark: 76.0% stays, and it asks for a pass mark.
9. Copy " 17.5 " with the spaces and paste it into Marks earned: 76.0% Pass.
10. Press Tab repeatedly: a blue outline moves earned → total → pass mark, then leaves the card.
11. Switch to dark mode and reload: the dark card is readable, and the fields reset with the pass mark at 70.
12. Phone: tapping a field opens a number keypad with a decimal point.
13. Phone: 16.08 of 23 with pass mark 69.9 shows "69.9%", "Pass", "Less than 0.01 marks above the pass mark", with no sideways scroll.
14. Phone: pass mark "-5" shows "Pass mark can't be negative.".

**Decisions for you:**
1. **Run the checklist and tell me the result.** "All pass", or the browser, step number and what you saw. When everything passes, the docs-writer marks S-1 to S-3 **Implemented**. Until then they stay "Not implemented", as the honesty rule requires.
2. Approve Gate 8 to start Stage 9 (release). That covers the README, the clean-clone audit, and the `v1.0.0` tag, which you'll create in the GitHub web UI because tag pushes are blocked here.

**Deliverables touched:** D1, D3, D5 and D6 are IN PROGRESS until your checklist is done.

**Time:** Sprint 2 ran 15:17–15:43 UTC (26 min).

**GitHub:** branch `main`, commit [`7094710`](https://github.com/Sabeekhann/Web-Calculator/commit/7094710), pushed: yes.

**Awaiting:** your checklist results, plus "approved" or corrections.

1	# Quiz score and pass-mark calculator — Sabee Khan
2	
3	## What the app is and who it is for
4	
5	A one-screen web calculator that turns raw quiz marks (for example 17.5 out of 23) into a percentage score, a clear Pass or Fail verdict against a pass mark, and how many marks the result is short of or above that pass mark. It is for two people on a compliance course: the **Learner**, who has had a quiz returned as raw marks and needs to know whether they passed and by how much before a resit deadline, and the **Instructor**, who marks short-answer assessments by hand and must record the same defensible percentage and verdict for every learner (see [app roles](docs/app-roles.md)). Mistyped or impossible entries, such as more marks earned than possible or a total of 0, get a plain message naming what to fix and no score.
6	
7	![The calculator showing 17.5 of 23 marks: 76.0%, Pass, 1.4 marks above the pass mark](docs/process/design/screenshots/final-1280-light.png)
8	
9	## Why this calculator
10	
11	Chosen by the product owner from three options (decision DEC-6; full comparison in the [product brief](docs/process/product-brief.md)):
12	
13	- **Fits the company:** learners and instructors are KnowledgeCity's everyday users.
14	- **Roles that differ:** the Learner wants a verdict and the gap to the pass mark; the Instructor wants a consistent, defensible percentage.
15	- **Edge cases come from the domain:** 0 possible marks (division by zero), marks earned above marks possible, rounding at the pass boundary (69.96% must never look like a 70% pass).
16	- **Small and safe for 2–4 hours:** 3 inputs, 3 Must stories, no currency or locale formatting.
17	- **Fresh:** it does not repeat an earlier bill-splitter attempt in this repository's history.
18	
19	## Prerequisites
20	
21	- **Node.js 20 LTS.** `.nvmrc` says `20` (run `nvm use` if you use nvm); `package.json` requires `"node": ">=20"`. CI runs on Node 20.
22	- **npm**, which comes with Node.js.
23	- **Git**, to clone the repository.
24	- No accounts, API keys, backend or cloud services. The app has no runtime dependencies.
25	
26	## Install and start
27	
28	```bash
29	git clone https://github.com/Sabeekhann/Web-Calculator.git
30	cd Web-Calculator/sabee-khan-calculator
31	npm ci            # npm install also works
32	npm run dev
33	```
34	
35	Open the URL Vite prints, normally <http://localhost:5173/>.
36	
37	Production build:
38	
39	```bash
40	npm run build     # type-check, then build into dist/
41	npm run preview   # serve dist/ at http://127.0.0.1:4173/
42	```
43	
44	## Running the tests
45	
46	**Unit tests (Vitest)**: 131 tests in `tests/unit/`, one file per story (S-1, S-2, S-3) plus the message catalogue.
47	
48	```bash
49	npm test
50	```
51	
52	**End-to-end tests (Playwright)**: 51 tests per engine, on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, run against the production build (Playwright builds it and starts `vite preview` itself).
53	
54	```bash
55	npx playwright install    # one time: downloads the Playwright browsers
56	npm run test:e2e
57	```
58	
59	| Spec file (`tests/e2e/`) | Tests | Covers |
60	|-----------|-------|--------|
61	| `shell.spec.ts` | 4 | Page title and heading, labelled inputs, idle state, no sideways scroll at 320 px |
62	| `S-1.spec.ts` | 8 | S-1 acceptance criteria: score and Pass/Fail verdict |
63	| `S-2.spec.ts` | 9 | S-2 acceptance criteria: marks short of or above the pass mark, plus no layout shift |
64	| `S-3.spec.ts` | 10 | S-3 acceptance criteria: error messages, plus no layout shift |
65	| `a11y.spec.ts` | 10 | axe scan for WCAG 2.2 AA in 5 states (idle, Pass, Fail, error, pass mark empty), light and dark |
66	| `edge.spec.ts` | 10 | Edge sweep: spaces, lone "." or "-", 400-digit input, pasted text, Enter key, reload, key-by-key typing, never NaN/Infinity/undefined/blank |
67

76	3. Enter **17.49** of **25**. Expect **69.9%** and **Fail**, never "70.0%". Then **17.5** of **25**: **70.0%**, **Pass**, "Exactly on the pass mark". (S-1, S-2 boundary)

80	7. Clear the pass mark. Expect 76.0% to stay, with "Enter a pass mark to see whether this is a pass or a fail." and no red message. (S-3)

89	- **Documentation first:** roles → jobs → stories with acceptance criteria → design → plan → code.

95	None.

97	## Assumptions
98	
99	Approved by the product owner (IDs match the [decision log](docs/process/decision-log.md)):
100	
101	- **A-1** A learner passes when the score is at or above the pass mark.
102	- **A-2** The verdict uses the exact, unrounded score, never the displayed value.
103	- **A-3** The score is shown to 1 decimal place, rounded down (69.96% → "69.9%", 2/3 → "66.6%"), so a failing score never looks like the pass mark.
104	- **A-4** Marks earned and total marks possible accept up to 2 decimal places, with a dot as the decimal separator.
105	- **A-5** Total marks possible is more than 0 and at most 1,000,000.
106	- **A-6** The pass mark starts at 70, can be changed, and accepts 0 to 100 with up to 1 decimal place.
107	- **A-7** Results update as you type; there is no Calculate button.
108	- **A-8** Marks earned can't be more than total marks possible (no bonus marks).
109	- **A-9** The gap to the pass mark is shown in marks, not percentage points.
110	- **A-10** Marks needed = pass mark ÷ 100 × total. A shortfall is rounded up and a surplus rounded down to 2 decimal places; a surplus under 0.01 shows "Less than 0.01 marks above the pass mark"; equal shows "Exactly on the pass mark".
111	- **A-11** Gap numbers drop trailing zeros ("0.60" → "0.6") and use comma thousands separators ("699,999.99"); "mark" is singular only for exactly 1.
112	- **A-12** An empty field (or only spaces) never shows an error: the result area asks for the missing entries; with no pass mark the score still shows and the verdict area asks for a pass mark.
113	- **A-13** Accepted numbers: digits with at most one dot (".5" and "5." are fine), leading zeros, surrounding spaces ignored. Anything else ("abc", "17,5", "$17", "1.2.3", "1e400", "+5") gets that field's not-a-number message.
114	- **A-14** A minus sign before a number, including "-0", gets that field's can't-be-negative message.
